body.en: The capstone of Calc III integrates vector fields — assignments of a vector to every point — along curves and across surfaces. Three great theorems (Green, Stokes, Divergence) tie these integrals back to the derivatives \( \nabla\cdot\mathbf{F} \) and \( \nabla\times\mathbf{F} \).

The line integral \( \displaystyle\int_C \mathbf{F}\cdot d\mathbf{r} \) measures the work a field \( \mathbf{F} \) does along a curve \( C \). A field is conservative when \( \mathbf{F}=\nabla f \) for some \( f \); then the integral is path-independent and equals \( f(\text{end})-f(\text{start}) \).

For a positively oriented simple closed curve \( C \) bounding a region \( R \) in the plane,

\[ \oint_C \big(P\,dx+Q\,dy\big)=\iint_{R}\Big(\frac{\partial Q}{\partial x}-\frac{\partial P}{\partial y}\Big)\,dA. \]

body.en:
Green's theorem generalizes in two directions. Stokes' theorem relates circulation around a boundary curve to the curl over a surface; the Divergence theorem relates outward flux through a closed surface to the divergence inside:

\[ \oint_C \mathbf{F}\cdot d\mathbf{r}=\iint_S (\nabla\times\mathbf{F})\cdot d\mathbf{S}, \qquad \iint_S \mathbf{F}\cdot d\mathbf{S}=\iiint_E (\nabla\cdot\mathbf{F})\,dV. \]

Evaluate \( \displaystyle\oint_C (-y\,dx+x\,dy) \) around the unit circle, counterclockwise.

Here \( P=-y,\ Q=x \), so \( Q_x-P_y=1-(-1)=2 \). By Green's theorem,

\[ \oint_C(-y\,dx+x\,dy)=\iint_{R}2\,dA=2(\text{area of disk})=2\pi. \]

Find the outward flux of \( \mathbf{F}=\langle x,y,z\rangle \) through the unit sphere.

Since \( \nabla\cdot\mathbf{F}=1+1+1=3 \), the Divergence theorem turns the surface flux into a volume integral over the unit ball \( E \):

\[ \iint_S \mathbf{F}\cdot d\mathbf{S}=\iiint_E 3\,dV=3\cdot\tfrac{4}{3}\pi=4\pi. \]

caption.en: Positively oriented (counterclockwise) closed boundary curve \(C\) enclosing planar region \(R\) for Green's Theorem.

body.en:
Green's Theorem Orientation: Green's Theorem \(\oint_C (P\,dx + Q\,dy) = \iint_R (Q_x - P_y)\,dA\) strictly requires a positively oriented (counterclockwise) boundary curve \(C\) keeping the region on the left. If traversing clockwise, you MUST insert a negative sign!

Conservative Vector Fields Checklist: A vector field \(\vec F = abla f\) has \( ext{curl}(\vec F) = \vec 0\). On simply connected domains: (1) Path independence \(\int_{C_1} = \int_{C_2}\); (2) Zero work around any closed loop: \(\oint_C \vec F \cdot d\vec r = 0\); (3) Fundamental Theorem for Line Integrals: \(\int_C abla f \cdot d\vec r = f(B) - f(A)\).

Divergence vs Curl: Divergence \( abla \cdot \vec F\) yields a scalar measuring net outflow; Curl \( abla imes \vec F\) yields a vector measuring rotational circulation.

question.en: Use Green's Theorem to evaluate \(\displaystyle\oint_C (3y\,dx + 5x\,dy)\) where \(C\) is the counterclockwise circle \(x^2 + y^2 = 4\).

solution.en:
Identify components: \(P = 3y\) and \(Q = 5x\).
Compute partial derivatives: \(\frac{\partial Q}{\partial x} = 5\) and \(\frac{\partial P}{\partial y} = 3\).
Apply Green's Theorem:
\[ \oint_C (3y\,dx + 5x\,dy) = \iint_R \left(\frac{\partial Q}{\partial x} - \frac{\partial P}{\partial y}\right)\,dA = \iint_R (5 - 3)\,dA = 2 \iint_R dA. \]
The region \(R\) is a disk of radius \(r = 2\), so its area is \(\pi(2^2) = 4\pi\).
Therefore, \(2 \iint_R dA = 2(4\pi) = 8\pi\).
